questions.q: A mass of 1 kg is executing SHM. Its displacement is given by $x=6.0\cos(100t+\pi/4)$ cm. What is the maximum kinetic energy?
questions.explanation: Amplitude A = 0.06 m, ω = 100 rad/s, so v$_{max}$ = Aω = 6 m/s. KE$_{max}$ = ½mv$_{max}^2$ = ½×1×36 = 18 J.

questions.q: The variations of kinetic energy K(x), potential energy U(x) and total energy as a function of displacement of a particle in SHM is as shown in the figure. The value of |x$_0$| is
questions.explanation: $K(x)=U(x)$ (curves cross) occurs when $\tfrac12 x^2=\tfrac12(A^2-x^2)$ i.e. $x=A/\sqrt2$; this is the marked point $x_0$.

questions.q: For a particle executing simple harmonic motion (SHM), at its mean position
options: Velocity is zero and acceleration is maximum
Velocity is maximum and acceleration is zero
Both velocity and acceleration are maximum
Both velocity and acceleration are zero
questions.explanation: At the mean position ($y=0$), $v=\omega\sqrt{A^2-y^2}$ is maximum while $a=-\omega^2y$ is zero.

questions.q: A block of mass m is connected to a light spring of force constant k. The system is placed inside a damping medium of damping constant b. The instantaneous values of displacement, acceleration and energy of the block are x, a and E respectively. The initial amplitude of oscillation is A and ω' is the angular frequency of oscillations. The incorrect expression related to the damped oscillations is
questions.explanation: The correct displacement equation for a damped oscillator is $x=Ae^{-\frac{bt}{2m}}\cos(\omega't+\phi)$; option D omits the time dependence and the factor 2 in the exponent, making it the incorrect expression.

questions.q: The displacement of a particle executing SHM is given by $X=3\sin\left[2\pi t+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]$ where 'x' is in metres and 't' is in seconds. The amplitude and maximum speed of the particle is
questions.explanation: Amplitude $A=3$ m, $\omega=2\pi$ rad/s; maximum speed $=A\omega=3\times2\pi=6\pi$ m/s.

questions.q: A pendulum oscillates simple harmonically if and only if (I) the size of the bob of pendulum is negligible in comparison with the length of the pendulum. (II) the angular amplitude is less than 10°.
questions.explanation: A simple pendulum behaves as a point mass (bob size negligible) and executes SHM only for small angular amplitudes (< 10°); both conditions are necessary.

questions.q: A piston is performing S.H.M. in the vertical direction with a frequency of 0.5 Hz. A block of 10 kg is placed on the piston. The maximum amplitude of the system such that the block remains in contact with the piston is
questions.explanation: The block loses contact when $\omega^2A = g$; with $\omega=2\pi(0.5)=\pi$ rad/s, $A = g/\omega^2 = 9.8/\pi^2 \approx 1$ m.

questions.q: Two simple pendulums A and B are made to oscillate simultaneously and it is found that A completes 10 oscillations in 20 sec and B completes 8 oscillations in 10 sec. The ratio of the lengths of A and B is
A particle executing SHM has a maximum speed of 0.5 ms$^{-1}$ and maximum acceleration of 1.0 ms$^{-2}$. The angular frequency of oscillation is
The ratio of kinetic energy to the potential energy of a particle executing SHM at a distance equal to half its amplitude, the distance being measured from its equilibrium position is
questions.explanation: PE $=\dfrac12 kx^2$ with $x=A/2$ gives PE $=\dfrac{kA^2}{8}$; total energy $E=\dfrac12 kA^2$, so KE $=E-$PE$=\dfrac{3kA^2}{8}$; KE:PE = 3:1.

questions.q: A 10 kg metal block is attached to a spring of spring constant 1000 Nm$^{-1}$. A block is displaced from equilibrium position by 10 cm and released. The maximum acceleration of the block is

From a fixed support, two small identical spheres are suspended by means of strings of length 1 m each. They are pulled aside as shown and then released. B is the mean position. Then the two spheres collide, [two identical pendulums of length 1 m hang from the same point; one is pulled to 30$^\circ$ from the vertical on one side and the other to 60$^\circ$ on the other side; B marks the common vertical mean position]
options: on the right side of B after some time
on the right side of B when the strings are inclined at 15$^\circ$ with B
questions.explanation: Both pendulums have the same length, so (for small-angle SHM) each takes a quarter period $T/4$ to swing to the mean position B, regardless of its release angle. $T=2\pi\sqrt{L/g}\approx2\text{ s}$, so $T/4\approx0.5\text{ s}$. (KEA's key also accepts option 3.)

questions.q: The circular motion of a particle with constant speed is
questions.explanation: It repeats identically after each revolution (periodic), but SHM requires oscillation along a straight line about a mean position with a restoring force proportional to displacement, which uniform circular motion does not have.

questions.q: A particle executes SHM with amplitude 0.2 m and time period 24 s. The time required for it to move from the mean position to a point 0.1 m from the mean position is
questions.explanation: $x=A\sin\omega t$ with $x=A/2$ gives $\sin\omega t=1/2$, so $\omega t=\pi/6$; with $\omega=2\pi/24=\pi/12$, t = 2 s.

questions.q: A particle executing a simple harmonic motion has a period of 6 sec. The time taken by the particle to move from the mean position to half the amplitude, starting from the mean position is .................
questions.explanation: $x=A\sin(\omega t)$; for $x=A/2$, $\sin(\omega t)=1/2 \Rightarrow \omega t=\pi/6 \Rightarrow t=T/12=6/12=0.5$ sec.
